start_here: Say to your AI: "Before I show test-piece, run the delivery gate at stage S5 and tell me which checks are still open." It runs tool:gate-a-pieces-delivery-checklist with the gate command.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON. For the delivery gate the row holds the delivery_gate rules the schema argument can point at.
alike: a config sheet or settings spreadsheet
a notes page of defaults per project

instructions: 1. Have a library with a schema (or a list:settings row holding it) whose delivery_gate names the checklist pool, the answers file, the stages and the rules, and a piece folder whose header lists its tags (the made-up film library in the test fixtures is a worked one). Pour the example settings rows into your own settings list (see pour).

2. Say to your AI: "Run the delivery gate on test-piece at S5". It reads the row with tools:list and runs python3 -I tools/keep-a-record-library-valid/do-work/keep_a_record_library.py --library <library> --schema <schema> gate <piece> --stage S5
3. Read every unanswered_must, failed_must and stale item to the person with the command that answers it (each carries an answer_with line). Exit 1 means something is still open.

4. Answer a check only with evidence you read, under your own name: python3 -I tools/keep-a-record-library-valid/do-work/keep_a_record_library.py --library <library> --schema <schema> answer <piece> --check S5.1 --answer pass --evidence "<file, number or list>" --by <name>. Never use a machine's name.
5. Run gate again: all_passed turns true when every routed MUST check has a pass row on the current bytes. Run audit-watch before linking anything into a watch folder.

worked_examples.title: Two open checks, answered, then the gate passes
worked_examples.ask: Before I show test-piece, which delivery checks are still open at S5?
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/keep-a-record-library-valid/read-data/delivery_gate.py and run for real on a copy of tools/keep-a-record-library-valid/test/fixtures/delivery with films/test-piece (SCRIPT.md header: medium video, source data:git, shape list, flags hf; film-gate.json {}): python3 -I tools/keep-a-record-library-valid/do-work/keep_a_record_library.py --library library --schema library/schema.json gate library/films/test-piece --stage S5; then two answer calls by Sam; then gate again.
worked_examples.hands_back: First gate, exit 1: {"all_passed": false, "stages": ["S5"], "tags": ["data", "data:git", "hf", "list", "video"], "problems": [], "failed_must": [], "at": "final", ...} with unanswered_must S5.1 ("The overlay lint has 0 errors.", verify "a listing") and S5.2 ("The picture renders in every aspect the header names."), each with an answer_with command. answer --check S5.1 --answer pass --evidence "overlay lint listing: 0 errors" --by Sam writes {"check_id": "S5.1", "answer": "pass", "evidence": "overlay lint listing: 0 errors", "by": "Sam", ...}; after both are answered the gate answers all_passed true with unanswered_must [] and failed_must [].

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for tool settings and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and list:settings as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
